note: Each numeric literal's parsed exponent is stored in the decNumber object that represents the input-controlled number.
The jq literal number wrapper receives the decNumber with the input-controlled exponent and later supplies it to comparisons.
The constant expression comparison in the input filter sends both numeric literals into jq's value comparison path during compilation.
Number comparison dispatch preserves the two literal number objects and forwards them to the decNumber comparison wrapper.
Both jq literal numbers are converted back to decNumber pointers and passed as lhs and rhs to decNumberCompare.
The comparison computes an exponent gap for alignment without first ensuring the gap is representable in the Int type.
The input exponents can make this subtraction exceed INT32_MAX before decUnitCompare receives the exp argument, triggering signed integer overflow.
